teaser.text: Diageo is a drinks company built around brands such as Johnnie Walker, Don Julio and Guinness. It earns money by making those brands desirable, supplying them through a complicated route to the customer and managing the cash tied up along the way.

sources.title: Diageo — Fiscal 27 Q1 Aide Memoire — 13 October 2026

stock.opening: Diageo's weighted price is 2,351.32 GBp in October 2027, with the bear case at 25%, the base case at 55% and the bull case at 20%. It hinges on demand improvement.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how Diageo makes money, who its rivals are, how management is responding, and what risks could change the outcome.

blocks.heading: Where could Diageo's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is 2,351.32 GBp in October 2027, implying a 37% return including dividends. The bear case has 25% probability; the base case has 55%. The bull case has 20%.

Probability-weighting gives 2,351.32 GBp in October 2027. It rises to 2,506.82 GBp in October 2028 and 2,695.33 GBp in October 2029. Including dividends, those outcomes represent returns of 37% and 49% from today’s 1,739.50 GBp. The third-year return is 62%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Diageo's forecast?

paragraphs.text: The base assumes broadly flat FY27 sales, savings-led margin recovery and later demand improvement. That follows guidance for broadly flat organic sales and low-to-mid-single-digit operating-profit growth. The bear falls from $3,398m in 2027 to $3,240m in 2028, then reaches $3,264m in 2029 as North America, China and tequila remain weak. The bull rises from $4,245m to $4,586m, then $4,957m, as Guinness grows, tequila stabilises and savings reach margins without reducing brand investment. Guinness’s recent growth supports that possibility, but FY26 organic sales fell 2.0%, making the base more credible than the bull.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Diageo really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow subtracts investment in factories, equipment and software from operating cash. It improved because capital spending fell, so the larger surplus does not represent an equally large improvement in trading. Diageo’s own measure also adds proceeds from asset sales. A stricter measure deducts lease payments and the economic cost of stock-based pay.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Diageo today?

paragraphs.text: The apparent bargain rests on a sharp difference between trailing and forward P/E. Trailing P/E uses the last year’s profit, while forward P/E uses an estimate of future profit. Diageo’s FY26 reported EPS was 78.1 US cents, while EPS before exceptional items was 165.3 US cents. A $1.5 billion impairment charge, principally involving Türkiye and Don Papa, depressed reported earnings. An impairment is an accounting reduction in an asset’s value, but it can also show that a brand or market has genuinely weakened.

dividend.title: Diageo dividend: cash coverage and yield
dividend.meta_description: Diageo dividend history, cash coverage, planned payout and current yield against the share price.
dividend.opening: Diageo pays a 50.00-US-cent annual dividend floor, down from 103.48 cents for fiscal 2025. Diageo generated $3,069 million of free cash flow in fiscal 2026 and had $1,059 million left after those payments.
dividend.closing: The full Diageo memo also examines Diageo's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Diageo pay shareholders over time?

paragraphs.text: The cash schedule shows the competing demands. Acquisitions used $23 million while business and asset sales brought in $304 million. Debt repayments were $3,147 million against $1,498 million issued. Cash still fell $374 million, and net debt ended at $19,991 million, above $16,620 million in fiscal 2022. The dividend reset formalised the change: Diageo adopted a 30.0%–50.0% earnings payout range with a 50.00-US-cent annual floor, down from 103.48 cents for fiscal 2025.

The base dividend holds at $0.50 in 2027 and rises to $0.52 in 2028. It reaches $0.55 in 2029. The bear holds $0.50 throughout, relying on the stated floor after the recent cut from $1.0348. The bull also starts at $0.50, then reaches $0.56 and $0.62 as cash flow improves. The $2,000m FY27 free-cash-flow target supports the floor, but debt reduction and exceptional costs limit faster increases.

blocks.heading: Is Diageo's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The position improved after buybacks stopped. In fiscal 2025, only $135 million remained after payments to both sets of shareholders. In fiscal 2026, free cash flow of $3,069 million left $1,059 million after those payments. Net capital expenditure was $1,181 million, down from $1,549 million, and included a $20 million investment in smaller-bottle capacity. Free cash flow already includes capital expenditure, so it should not be deducted again.

paragraphs.text: Management expects broadly flat organic net sales for the year to June 2027, low-to-mid-single-digit organic operating profit growth and a mid-single-digit North American sales decline. It targets $2,000 million of free cash flow and 2.75x leverage. Exceptional cash costs are expected to reach $850 million. Through fiscal 2029, management targets $8,000 million of cumulative free cash flow after exceptional cash costs.

The base case would strengthen if FY27 delivers broadly flat organic sales and low-to-mid-single-digit operating-profit growth, followed by stabilising North American demand. Free cash flow that funds the dividend while reducing leverage through FY29 would support the assumed multiple.
